title: Xia
capsule: Xia (often called Hu Xia or Helian Xia) was one of the Sixteen Kingdoms of northern China, founded in 407 by Helian Bobo (originally Liu Bobo), a chieftain of the Tiefu Xiongnu who claimed descent from the ancient Xia dynasty and styled himself Heavenly King and Grand Chanyu. From a base in the Ordos region he built the fortress-capital of Tongwancheng around 413 at the edge of the Mu Us Desert and in 418 seized Chang'an and the Guanzhong plain from the Eastern Jin general Liu Yu's overextended forces. After Helian Bobo's death in 425 the Northern Wei dismantled the state piece by piece, capturing Tongwancheng in 427 and the emperor Helian Chang in 428; the last ruler, Helian Ding, was seized by the Tuyuhun in 431 and handed to Wei, ending the kingdom.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core territory along the Hexi Corridor is well-defined by Chinese dynastic cartography and administrative records; nomadic steppe boundaries to the north and northwest are approximate and inferred from military campaign accounts.
